papers.title: Quantity-Level FDIA in SDR-Based P2P Energy Trading: Cyber-Economic Impact and Pre-Clearing Detection
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the cyber-economic impact and pre-clearing detectability of false data injection attacks (FDIAs) in peer-to-peer (P2P) energy trading among interconnected microgrids. In the proposed cyber-economic framework, load and photovoltaic profiles drive a sequential 15-minute market with deterministic double-sided proportional (pro-rata) allocation and supply-to-demand-ratio (SDR) pricing, while true physical injections are separated from communicated market quantities. The framework is evaluated through a multi-microgrid case study over 69,904 market-aligned states, for which all AC power-flow solutions converged and voltages remained within 0.98999-1.04369 per unit. Healthy local exchange reached 1,159.66 MWh and generated USD 92,772.62 of community benefit. Bias, scaling, and ramp attacks modify only one microgrid's communicated quantity, altering the settlement price, P2P allocation, scheduled residual-grid exchange, participant financial outcomes, and benefit fairness, while true feeder injections remain unchanged. Role-specific random forest, statistical threshold, and score-fusion detectors are compared using only information available before clearing. Pooled sample-level detection rates range from 7.82% to 12.14%, with false-alarm rates from 4.69% to 7.70% and role dependence. In the investigated case study, measurable downstream economic distortion and low pre-clearing detectability coexist under bounded quantity manipulation.

papers.title: RadioWorld: Transferring World Models to Radio-Frequency Radiance Fields
papers.abstract: Electromagnetic (EM) wave propagation in the physical world constitutes a Radio-Frequency (RF) radiance field, providing rich information for 6G communication and sensing. However, existing neural RF field methods suffer from three fundamental limitations: (1) they predominantly rely on per-scene optimization and cannot generalize to unseen scenes; (2) they require costly reference RF measurements in each target scene; and (3) they degrade severely when extrapolating beyond the vicinity of reference measurements. To overcome these limitations, we present RadioWorld, a general framework that adapts a world model to synthesize RF radiance fields directly from physical scene geometry and transceiver locations, without requiring any reference RF measurements at inference. Specifically, RadioWorld couples two specialized modules within a dual-stream Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) architecture: a Scene-Understanding Transformer that encodes 3D scene geometry and transceiver locations to extract environment-aware global EM propagation features, and a Field-Generation Transformer that attends to these features to synthesize the RF radiance field with the local query conditions. We also establish UrbanRF-Bench, a large-scale ray-traced benchmark spanning 657 urban scenes and 32,850 RF radiance fields across seven global cities. Extensive experiments demonstrate that RadioWorld significantly outperforms specialized baselines and accurately synthesizes RF fields at arbitrary locations in unseen cities. Code, datasets, and checkpoints will be released upon acceptance.

papers.title: VEGA: A Scalable Software-Hardware Co-design for Genome Alignment using RVV Extension
papers.abstract: Dynamic programming (DP)-based genome sequence analysis is fundamental to computational genomics, but it remains computationally intensive as genomic data volumes continue to outpace Moore's Law. Existing hardware accelerators often sacrifice programmability and scalability across diverse alignment algorithms. In this work, we present VEGA, a scalable software-hardware co-design that accelerates genome alignment using RISC-V Vector extensions. VEGA introduces specialized vector instructions and three key innovations: a Forefront Stationary dataflow that minimizes off-chip memory access, intersequence parallelism that maximizes SIMD lane utilization, and custom ISA extensions that accelerate core alignment operations. Evaluations show that VEGA achieves up to 15.1x and 9.7x speedups for Edit Distance and Smith-Waterman algorithms over the Ara2-RVV vector baseline, sustaining 10.2x and 6.7x gains for 10kbp sequences. Post-synthesis results indicate only 1.0% area overhead compared to a standard RISC-V core, with performance-per-area efficiency rivaling specialized ASICs. VEGA thus achieves a balanced advancement in efficiency, programmability, and scalability for genome sequence alignment.

papers.title: Denoised but Not Improved: What EEG Denoising Does to a Downstream Task
papers.abstract: Scalp electroencephalography (EEG) is routinely denoised before it reaches a downstream model, and the denoising literature scores a method by how closely its output matches a clean reference waveform. That reference does not exist for real scalp recordings: it is synthesized by adding artifact templates to signals merely presumed clean, and even an exact separation would return cortical activity blurred by volume conduction rather than the activity itself. Fidelity to it is therefore an unvalidatable objective, and whether it predicts any downstream benefit has gone largely unexamined. We report an audit that examines it. Holding a seizure-detection pipeline fixed and varying only the preprocessing stage, we find that five standard denoising methods, spanning analytic, cross-channel and supervised deep families, all fail to improve on the unprocessed signal, and most degrade it. To say what such a stage must instead do, we formalize a label-only, classifier-free probe that reads it by the separability geometry it induces on task-relevant features, decomposing any change into a between-class distance and a within-class scatter term. On a transform that does improve the task, the probe attributes the entire gain to a roughly one-quarter reduction of within-class scatter, with class separation statistically unchanged. What a downstream model benefits from is therefore variance suppression on task-relevant structure, which waveform-fidelity metrics neither measure nor reward.

papers.title: Near-Field Physical-Layer Authentication Under Noisy Enrollment
papers.abstract: In near-field physical-layer authentication (PLA), the receiver estimates a spatial reference from noisy enrollment pilots. With a fixed residual-energy threshold, even a small reference error can cause the false rejection (FR) probability to approach one as the received energy increases. We derive the distribution of the overlap between the true and enrolled spatial directions and use it to calibrate a test based on the aligned energy and the residual-to-aligned energy ratio. The calibration bounds FR for arbitrary regional gains and all legitimate received energies above a prescribed minimum. For a fixed enrolled reference, we reduce the problem of finding the maximum acceptance probability of a multi-antenna attacker to a one-dimensional search. We also derive a pre-enrollment upper bound that holds when the attacker chooses its precoder after observing the enrolled reference. For a single region and a fixed angular threshold, the enrollment energy sufficient to preserve angular separation grows inversely with the square of the available angular margin. In the numerical study with 128 receive elements at 28 GHz, the FR upper bound was 0.9984, including the enrollment outage allowance. At a regional phase perturbation of 20, four regions provided the best trade-off among the tested partitions: its simulated FR was 0.1442, while its false acceptance (FA) at 9 m was 1.084 under the fixed transmit-energy setting.

papers.title: One UWB Radar, Many Views: Comparing and Fusing Signal Representations for Human Activity Recognition
papers.abstract: IEEE 802.15.4z-compliant impulse-radio ultra-wideband (IR-UWB) transceivers are increasingly built into consumer devices, enabling contactless, privacy-preserving human activity recognition (HAR) in healthcare. Before activity classification, the signal is typically converted into range-time, range-Doppler, or time-Doppler maps, each exposing different spatial and motion cues. Existing comparisons often apply shared processing across representations, leaving it unclear whether their rankings hold after independent tuning. It is also unknown whether rankings and fusion gains generalize across environments and activities, and at what computational cost. Consequently, practitioners lack guidance on which representation and processing suit a given HAR deployment. We release an open dataset of raw IR-UWB measurements collected by a ceiling-mounted radar from 44 participants during scripted activity sequences in 12 layouts across two bedrooms. Using a statistically guided, staged search, we independently tune each representation across five processing and deployment settings. We then compare individual and fused performance under layout and room shifts and quantify computational cost. Across over 1{,}000 cross-validated models, independent tuning proves essential, as optimal processing differs per representation and processing choices shift macro-F1 by up to 26 points, four times the gap between representations. Once tuned, the range-Doppler map leads for unseen layouts (85.1\% macro-F1), while time-Doppler map does for unseen rooms (72.7\%). Fusing all three maps raises these scores to 89.1\% and 80.0\%, respectively. Lower sampling rates and narrower Doppler bands reduce latency by 38--51\% with at most a 1.5-point macro-F1 loss. The best representation for UWB HAR is therefore a deployment decision, not a fixed property.

papers.title: PsyDrift: Healthy-Reference Latent Diffusion for Anomaly Scoring in Autism Spectrum Disorder
papers.abstract: Individual heterogeneity and acquisition-site variability complicate neuroimaging-based characterization of autism spectrum disorder (ASD). We propose PsyDrift, combining ASD/healthy-control-supervised functional-connectivity representations with healthy-reference latent diffusion. An encoder produces 128-dimensional representations, and a denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM) learns exclusively from healthy training latents. Distance from a diffusion-denoised reconstruction provides a continuous deviation score. We evaluate 1,102 subjects from all 20 ABIDE-I sites using five-seed leave-one-site-out cross-validation. The classifier and DDPM achieve mean-site AUROCs of $0.798 \pm 0.003$ and $0.718 \pm 0.013$, respectively; uncertainties denote seed standard deviations. Matched healthy-reference scorers on the same representation achieve 0.68-0.71; the statistical significance of diffusion's modest numerical advantage remains unestablished. Within ASD, scores show weak associations with ADOS Total (Spearman $\rho = 0.108$, $p = 0.038$) and full-scale IQ ($\rho = -0.138$, $p = 0.002$), without adjustment for age, sex, site, or head motion. Frozen evaluation without retraining or hyperparameter adaptation yields pooled AUROCs of 0.69 on ABIDE-II and 0.61 on ADHD-200, providing preliminary evidence of cross-cohort and cross-disorder transfer. These results demonstrate healthy-reference deviation scoring within an ASD-supervised representation; incremental predictive and clinical value remains unestablished.

papers.title: Implicit Neural Representation for 3D Radio Map Compression in Low-Altitude Environments
papers.abstract: Low-altitude wireless networks require accurate 3D radio maps (RMs) to support environment-aware communication. However, due to the extensive spatial coverage and multi-modal channel representations, 3D RMs usually incur prohibitive storage and transmission overhead, making efficient compression highly desirable. In this paper, we propose NeRM3D, an implicit neural representation (INR)-based framework for compact 3D RM compression. Specifically, NeRM3D represents the entire 3D RM as a lightweight neural network that maps discrete height values to corresponding RM slices, thereby encoding the RM into a compact neural network. To effectively model the volumetric spatial structure of 3D RMs, NeRM3D jointly integrates horizontal embeddings with height-aware modulation, enabling efficient extraction and fusion of spatial correlations across different vertical layers and channel modalities. Experimental results demonstrate that NeRM3D achieves competitive compression performance with low complexity and decoding latency, making it suitable for resource-constrained devices.

papers.title: Inferring behind-the-meter demand components from net load via inverse optimization
papers.abstract: Understanding and forecasting electricity demand responses to price signals is essential to support the operational decisions of system operators, retailers, and regulators. Traditional time series and machine learning approaches have performed well under stable consumption patterns. However, the rise of active consumers with flexible assets, such as solar-plus-storage systems and electric vehicles, introduces new complexities. These consumers exhibit behind-the-meter behavior that is generally unobservable to system operators and retailers, who can typically only measure net demand at the boundary meters which are located at the connection points to the grid. Net demand reflects the aggregate of baseload consumption, flexible load shifting, and self-generation, all of which may respond nonlinearly to market prices. As these unobservable components grow, existing forecasting models may fail to capture the true dynamics of consumer behavior. This work develops and implements a data-driven inverse optimization framework to reveal behind-the-meter consumption patterns using only net demand data. By analyzing net demand as revealed at the grid connection point, we estimate parameters for a latent optimization model, enabling predictions that infer the unobservable components. This enables more accurate point and probabilistic forecasting of electricity demand under varying price signals. Thus, it provides actionable insights for system operators to improve local congestion management and flexibility extraction, as well as for retailers and aggregators, who could thereby optimize operations and tariffs to leverage consumer flexibility. We validate the methodology using real-world data, demonstrating improved forecasting accuracy over leading machine learning and time-series benchmarks.

papers.title: PPGFlowECG: Latent Rectified Flow with Cross-Modal Encoding for PPG-Guided ECG Generation and Cardiovascular Disease Detection
papers.abstract: Electrocardiography (ECG) is the clinical gold standard for cardiovascular disease (CVD) assessment, yet continuous monitoring is constrained by the need for dedicated hardware and trained personnel. Photoplethysmography (PPG) is ubiquitous in wearable devices and readily scalable, but it lacks electrophysiological specificity, limiting diagnostic reliability. While generative methods aim to translate PPG into clinically useful ECG signals, existing approaches are limited by the misalignment of physiological semantics in generative models and the complexity of modeling in high-dimensional signals. To address these limitations, we propose PPGFlowECG, a two-stage framework that aligns PPG and ECG in a shared latent space using the CardioAlign Encoder and then synthesizes ECGs with latent rectified flow. We further provide a formal analysis of this coupling, showing that the CardioAlign Encoder is necessary to guarantee stable and semantically consistent ECG synthesis under our formulation. Extensive experiments on four datasets demonstrate improved synthesis fidelity and downstream diagnostic utility. These results indicate that PPGFlowECG supports scalable, wearable-first CVD screening when standard ECG acquisition is unavailable.

papers.title: Probabilistic Risk Sensitivity and Loss Aversion in Cumulative Prospect Theory
papers.abstract: This paper develops a binary-gamble framework for characterizing risk sensitivity and loss aversion in Cumulative Prospect Theory (CPT). The proposed probabilistic risk-sensitivity metric is defined as a probability-threshold ratio that determines acceptance and preference thresholds in choice problems involving either a certain outcome and a binary gamble or two binary gambles. We show how standard notions of symmetric and non-symmetric bet aversion can be recovered within this framework, and we compare the resulting threshold-based conditions with utility premia, probability premia, and Arrow-Pratt curvature measures. The analysis clarifies when these criteria coincide and when they diverge, particularly for increasing aversion conditions, binary gambles with unequal probability distributions, and settings involving probability weighting functions. We also identify technical restrictions that arise when CPT-utility functions are used to represent loss aversion at the reference point. The resulting framework provides a decision-theoretic interpretation of risk sensitivity that is directly tied to probability thresholds and complements existing premium-based approaches.

papers.title: Sheaf-Based Federated Representation Learning
papers.abstract: Heterogeneous federated systems require agents to learn and exchange informative representations despite differences in data distributions, model architectures, and latent dimensionalities. We propose Sheaf-based Federated Representation Learning (SFRL), a framework that jointly learns and aligns heterogeneous latent representations without sharing parameters, labels, or a single latent space. SFRL relates agent-specific latent spaces through learnable orthogonal transformations and isometric embeddings, promoting consistency via a sheaf-Laplacian gluing regularizer evaluated on a shared set of pilot samples. We develop Sheaf-FRL, a decentralized alternating algorithm combining local gradient updates with closed-form Procrustes updates of the alignment maps, and establish convergence guarantees in deterministic and stochastic settings. On collaborative classification with semantic communication across four datasets, under model and data heterogeneity, Sheaf-FRL improves communication accuracy over federated baselines at no cost in private accuracy, and is more robust to latent-space compression.

papers.title: StreamingDPD: A 1.28-GSa/s Instantaneous-Power-Gated Depthwise TCN Accelerator for Real-Time 320-MHz Digital Predistortion
papers.abstract: State feedback between successive samples limits the streaming throughput of recurrent neural networks for digital predistortion (DPD). We present StreamingDPD, an accelerator that processes 320-MHz signals at 1.28 GSa/s. Its 207-parameter instantaneous-power-gated depthwise temporal convolutional network (IPG-DWTCN) uses $|x[n]|^2$ to gate feature channels and causal dilated depthwise convolutions to model power amplifier memory. The network maps to a spatially unrolled fixed-point pipeline with shift-based quadratic activations and layer-wise mixed precision, sustaining one complex sample per cycle per lane. Its algorithmic cost is 554 floating-point operations per complex sample, 30.1% fewer than the recurrent baseline with the best linearization performance. In RF playback measurements on three power amplifiers driven by 40- to 320-MHz Wi-Fi 6/7 and 5G NR waveforms, IPG-DWTCN achieves the lowest mean adjacent-channel power ratio (ACPR) and ranks first or ties for first in mean error vector magnitude (EVM) against five neural baselines of comparable size. Four-lane FPGA hardware-in-the-loop tests on a 320-MHz 4096-QAM Wi-Fi 7 waveform achieve -45.82 dBc ACPR and -42.94 dB EVM at 1.28 GSa/s. At the same sample rate, post-layout evaluation of a single-lane 12-nm FinFET ASIC yields a 0.10 mm$^2$ core, a 52-cycle (40.63 ns) latency, and an estimated typical-corner power of 142.21 mW (111.10 pJ/sample). Relative to the prior 22-nm recurrent DPD ASIC, the design provides 5.1 times the throughput at about one-seventh the energy per sample.

papers.title: Distributed Multimodal Monitoring and Prediction for PV Asset and Site Conditions
papers.abstract: Utility-scale photovoltaic (PV) monitoring remains fragmented: electrical performance, structural condition and vegetation management are typically assessed through separate workflows, making it difficult to relate changes in energy performance to the local physical and environmental conditions experienced by individual modules. We propose a distributed multimodal monitoring and prediction framework that combines mechanical, optical, electrical, and microclimate measurements at the string level. Rather than treating these measurements as independent sensor streams, the framework uses them to derive higher-level indicators of asset and site condition, including quantities that are not directly instrumented. We designed and installed four compact wireless nodes attached directly to the rear of PV modules for a three-month pilot study to demonstrate module-level monitoring. From low-cost multimodal measurements, the system detected vegetation-management events, predicted wind speed from module vibration on unseen data, and extracted repeatable structural-frequency fingerprints associated with individual module locations. These preliminary results demonstrate a pathway from distributed monitoring toward predictive PV asset management, where multimodal observations can be used to predict or estimate otherwise unobserved operating and structural states, identify emerging changes earlier, and provide more granular intelligence than plant-level electrical monitoring or periodic inspection alone.

papers.title: Benchmarking EEG feature families for ADHD research in children and adolescents: performance and explainability across attention tasks
papers.abstract: Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder varies in presentation. Diagnosis requires clinical and developmental assessment. Reproducible electroencephalography measures may complement clinical and behavioural characterisation, but differing feature definitions and evaluation methods hinder comparison. We compared seven feature families and four combinations across attention tasks and assessed the stability of held-out explanations. Two serious games yielded four overlapping attention-task cohorts of 123-140 participants each. Repeated nested participant-held-out evaluation assessed recruitment-group discrimination. Exploratory paired participant-cluster bootstrap tests corrected for multiplicity in two separate families: 72 individual-task contrasts and 18 fusion contrasts. For eight configurations selected after inspecting predictive results, we explained held-out native probabilities before calibration. In the strongest task context, the highest configuration mean AUROC over three repetitions was 0.773, with a fixed-prediction 95% interval of 0.692-0.854 unadjusted for selecting the maximum. Precision, sensitivity and specificity were 0.740, 0.556 and 0.861. In that task, the paired AUROC difference for connectivity minus spectral features averaged +0.2083 across six classifiers and the common 8 s and 16 s durations, with pointwise 95% CI 0.1076-0.3072 and adjusted p = 0.0036. F4-AF4 beta-band coherence led repetition-level attribution summaries in five selected procedures and was selected in every fit. Other contexts showed weaker discrimination and less consistent retention of leading scientific inputs. No general classifier winner emerged. Connectivity and its recurring coherence input warrant independent replication, but do not justify a universal feature recommendation. These exploratory findings do not establish causal task effects, disease mechanisms or diagnostic validity.

papers.title: Operating-Condition Normalization in C-MAPSS: Matched Historical Baselines, Multi-Seed Robustness, and Prognostic-Score Trade-offs
papers.abstract: Operating-state changes can obscure turbofan degradation signals, but a reduction in remaining-useful-life (RUL) error after condition-wise standardization may reflect weaknesses of the comparison features instead of a unique benefit of normalization. A controlled retrospective audit examines NASA C-MAPSS FD002 and FD004 with engine-disjoint folds, raw condition identifiers, two constructions of causal history, early-life baselines, and continuous operating-setting correction. Ridge regression, random forests and XGBoost are compared under explicit training-engine-only fitting rules. The previously reported XGBoost FD004 terminal RMSE decreased from 30.38 to 29.08 cycles following six-condition standardization; however, raw sensor values accompanied by condition-matched histories and condition identifiers achieved 28.09 cycles, reversing the naive point estimate ranking, although the paired-engine interval spans zero. For FD002, normalized XGBoost reduced terminal RMSE yet increased the asymmetric NASA score (12,616 to 13,289). Additional model-seed, condition count, RUL-cap, grouped-validation and explanation checks test sensitivity rather than postulating a universally optimal representation. The six clusters reproduce known simulator operating regimes; no new condition discovery algorithm, causal diagnostic method, or field ready prognostic system is claimed. Since the official test endpoints were also used in earlier exploratory comparisons, all newly examined alternatives are reported as retrospective benchmark evidence, not as results from a pristine confirmatory holdout.

papers.title: R2WM: Recursive Reasoning Wireless Model for Long-Horizon mmWave Beam Prediction
papers.abstract: Long-horizon beam prediction aims to extend beam-training intervals while supporting beam alignment in mobile millimeter-wave systems. Although pretrained large models can improve prediction over compact recurrent baselines, their large backbones impose substantial storage and computing requirements. To address this limitation, we propose a recursive reasoning wireless model (R2WM). Given a fixed history of beam indices and angles of departure (AoDs), R2WM repeatedly updates coupled latent and prediction states using a shared causal-attention backbone before jointly decoding the future beam indices. Backbone reuse increases computational depth at fixed parameter count. In the standard 10-step DeepMIMO setting, R2WM achieves an average normalized beamforming gain of 0.9597, compared with 0.8629 for the prompt-as-prefix large language model, with 99.1% fewer parameters and 59.1% fewer counted floating-point operations. Transfer experiments show that R2WM retains normalized gain under the tested carrier-frequency and antenna-count changes, while its beam-index-only variant retains gain under the tested base-station change. Component ablations show higher gains with historical AoD conditioning and causal attention. Recursion analysis reveals a gain-computation trade-off across separately trained configurations with the same parameter count. An additional comparison with a nonrecursive Transformer of similar parameter count shows higher gain for R2WM at greater computational cost. These results support accurate long-horizon beam prediction without a large pretrained backbone.

papers.title: Beyond Raw IQ: Compact Semantic Representations for Task Oriented Automatic Modulation Classification
papers.abstract: Automatic modulation classification (AMC) is an important component of modern wireless communication systems, but conventional signal representations can be expensive to store, process, and communicate, particularly under noisy channel conditions. This work investigates whether learned semantic representations can provide a compact alternative to high-dimensional in-phase and quadrature (IQ) representations while retaining robustness to noise. Starting from a 2048-dimensional IQ representation, we evaluate learned semantic representations with dimensions of 4, 8, 16, 32, and 64. Across the evaluated configurations, a 16-dimensional representation provides the strongest overall trade-off between classification performance, robustness, and representation size. The resulting representation achieves a 128x compression ratio and a 99.22% reduction in dimensionality. We further evaluate representation stability across signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs), compare semantic representations with a raw-IQ CNN, analyze per-class robustness, and perform five-seed validation. The five-seed evaluation produces an average accuracy of (49.22 +- 0.52)% and Macro-F1 of (49.27 +- 0.53)% across the evaluated SNR range. These results indicate that learned semantic compression can produce a substan- tially smaller representation while preserving useful classification information and improving geometric stability under noise.

papers.title: FAS-Assisted Self-Interference Mitigation for In-Band Full-Duplex Communications
papers.abstract: In-band full-duplex (IBFD) communication relies on effective self-interference cancellation (SIC) to overcome the strong loopback self-interference (SI). While fluid antenna system (FAS)-assisted SIC offers superior SI suppression by dynamically selecting the FAS port to minimize the residual SI power, it incurs high pilot overhead to acquire channel state information (CSI) for both forward and loopback channels. This raises the question of whether forward channel CSI is necessary for effective SI mitigation. To address this challenge, we propose a pilot-efficient FAS-assisted SI mitigation (FAS-SIM) approach that selects the FAS port solely based on the loopback SI channel. Theoretical performance analysis of the forward signal is provided. Numerical results then reveal that FAS-SIM achieves SI suppression and a forward-link rate comparable to the conventional method, while reducing port-selection training overhead by 50%, offering a low-overhead solution for IBFD communications.

papers.title: From Footprints to Service Regions: Modeling and Analysis of Dense LEO Satellite Networks Using an Orbit-Aware Cox Point Process
papers.abstract: In dense low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite networks, several accessible satellites cover the same location. A footprint therefore identifies where communication is feasible but does not determine which satellite serves each user. The service region of a satellite, namely the set of locations it serves, governs satellite load, resource sharing, and user throughput. Using an orbit-aware Cox point process on a common orbital shell, we model each service region as the intersection of a satellite's spherical-cap footprint and its spherical Voronoi cell under nearest-satellite association. We then use Palm calculus to derive exact expressions for the mean area and perimeter and a coverage--load identity. After coverage saturates, mean area and load decrease inversely with population. In contrast, adding satellites along existing orbits leaves a positive limiting mean perimeter. We connect this geometry to an approximate noise-limited user rate. Along the tested densification paths, the increase in user rate comes mainly from the decrease in mean satellite load rather than from the improvement of the serving link. We also compare the model with Walker constellations with Starlink-type parameters, using Cox parameters matched to the local orbit and satellite densities at each latitude. The model reproduces the mean area and perimeter of these constellations over broad latitude ranges, with larger differences near component maximum latitudes. These results show that service-region geometry, and hence satellite load and user rate, depend not only on the total satellite population but also on its allocation across orbital planes.

papers.title: SleepXA: Composing Pretrained Neural and Cardiac Foundation Models for Sleep Representation Learning
papers.abstract: Physiological signals recorded during sleep provide synchronized views of neural, cardiac, respiratory, and other bodily systems, while preserving modality-specific information. Existing EEG and ECG foundation models already capture rich but distinct physiological structure, motivating an alternative to training a multimodal sleep model from scratch: composing existing pretrained models. We introduce SleepXA, a framework that uses synchronized polysomnography (PSG) to compose independently pretrained neural and cardiac foundation models. SleepXA combines pretrained EEG and ECG encoders with lightweight encoders for additional PSG modalities, and learns shared and modality-specific representations through sleep-guided alignment. We pretrain SleepXA on 9,230 overnight PSG recordings from three large cohorts and evaluate it on 27 downstream tasks spanning sleep representation, clinical and disease prediction, and daytime physiological transfer. SleepXA ranks among the top two methods on 22 of 27 tasks. Controlled experiments further show consistent benefits across sensor configurations and EEG-ECG backbone choices, while pretrained initialization outperforms architecture-matched training from scratch and SleepXA surpasses alternative multimodal composition strategies. These results suggest that synchronized multimodal physiology can serve as a natural interface for composing existing physiological foundation models, yielding reusable representations that extend beyond sleep to clinical and daytime physiological settings.

papers.title: Black-Box Comparator-Adaptive Network Regret
papers.abstract: We study comparator-adaptive decentralized online learning with network regret, which evaluates each node's prediction on the loss of every node in the network. We show that existing gossip-based algorithms are fundamentally limited for this task, and cannot achieve sublinear network regret with only one gossip step per decision round. To prove this, we construct a two-node counterexample, which shows that gossip-based algorithms can produce exponential regret despite bounded disagreement, resolving a previously open question in the literature. We then introduce a black-box reduction, which uses local learners with sublinear comparator-adaptive regret to obtain sublinear comparator-adaptive network regret. Each node exchanges predictions with its neighbors once per decision round, and a universal choice of edge weights works on every connected undirected graph without graph preprocessing. We also characterize admissible edge weights and show how weights adapted to the graph improve the regret bound. For example, for the complete graph, this improvement is quadratic in the number of nodes. Experiments on synthetic and real-world data illustrate the counterexamples we propose and compare the reduction with decentralized baselines.

papers.title: Adaptive Beamforming Using One-Bit Data Samples for Covariance Estimation
papers.abstract: The use of one-bit quantized complex-valued data samples enables efficient distributed computation of an array data covariance. This reduced complexity covariance estimate can be used for adaptive beamforming, but requires careful diagonal loading and results in lower performance compared to a full-precision approach. Two main approaches are presented: a covariance matrix built out of complex one-bit data samples, and a ``hybrid'' cross-covariance between the one-bit data and the full precision data. Signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) estimates for the associated population and finite-sample matrices are derived and compared to the full precision results using tools from linear algebra and statistics. Many strong, well-separated interferers with low overlap with the signal of interest are assumed throughout, none of them dominant.

papers.title: DRU-Mixer: An Explainable Dilated Recurrent Unit-Based Mixer Model with Focal Loss for EEG-Based Interictal Epileptiform Discharges Detection
papers.abstract: Interictal epileptiform discharges (IED) have been identified as a core electroencephalogram (EEG) biomarker in diagnosing epilepsy patients. However, automatic detection and classification of IED require significant effort by human experts and can be prone to inter-rater variability. This paper presents Dilated Recurrent Units (DRU)-Mixer, a deep learning network to automate the process of identifying and classifying IED based on EEG recordings. The proposed architecture comprises a convolutional front end for extracting local features, dilated recurrent units modeling the temporal relationship between EEG signals, and mixer modules for token- and channel-level representation learning. DRU-Mixer was trained to perform (i) binary classification of IED/Non-IED segments and (ii) multiclass classification of regional IED types. For binary classification, DRU-Mixer showed 95.19% accuracy, 72.76% precision, 82.31% recall, 96.61% specificity, and 77.24% F1-score. For multiclass classification, the proposed network achieved strong sensitivity between 74.8% and 89.2%, as well as precision between 70.5% and 86.3%. Sensitivity-oriented analysis of the results shows that, for 70% sensitivity, DRU-Mixer provided 83.8% precision and 98.5% specificity outperforming VGGEEG and VGGSleep models and being on par with vEpiNet model. Interpretability of the model's results was estimated through occlusion mapping technique, which was used to highlight time intervals and EEG channels providing maximal contribution to the prediction. Maps generated by the technique show specific patterns for IED and Non-IED indicating that the model utilizes structured channel-time features corresponding to the presence of epileptiform activity.

papers.title: A Generalized Framework for Structured Low-Rank Approximation and Completion
papers.abstract: We formulate a generalized version of SLRA, consisting of general affine constraints, which subsumes the problems of structured low-rank matrix approximation and completion as special cases. We characterize its critical points and propose an algorithm to approximately solve the general problem. Finally, we demonstrate the performance of the proposed algorithm for stock-price forecasting, computing approximate gcd of polynomials with noisy coefficients, and time-series denoising.

papers.title: Asynchronous Uplink Rate Splitting Multiple Access
papers.abstract: We study a two-user uplink system in which each user splits its message into layers and transmits them with deliberately chosen timing offsets, a scheme we call asynchronous rate splitting (A-RS). We show that timing offsets make the layers distinguishable only in the excess band of the pulse, where two spectral aliases overlap. For a root-raised-cosine pulse, the rate for every subset of layers has a scalar closed form that depends on the offsets through a single timing dispersion term. For fixed layer spectra and timing offsets, the achievable two-user rate region is a pentagon. Its two maximum-sum-rate corners are attained by successive interference cancellation that combines all matched-filter outputs at each decoding stage. Two layers per user, separated by half a symbol, are optimal for any delay between the users, and the spectrum of the user decoded last is a water-filling nested inside the water-filling of the total power. At high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), the optimal spectrum has twice the density in the excess band. By using the excess bandwidth of the pulse, which synchronous transmission leaves unused, A-RS achieves rate pairs outside the regions of both synchronous and asynchronous non-orthogonal multiple access. We implement a practical system with low-density parity-check codes which gives the weaker user $0.97$ bits per symbol more than any single-stream scheme at the same SNR.

papers.title: Twisted Block Particle Filters: A Local Particle-System Change of Measure for High-Dimensional State-Space Models
papers.abstract: Block particle filters mitigate weight degeneracy in high-dimensional state-space models, but their normalizer estimates can remain highly variable. We introduce a twisted block particle filter (TBPF) that incorporates predictive guidance through an exact change of measure at blockwise resampling. The method guide-tilts one uniformly selected offspring per block, leaves the state-transition kernel unchanged, and computes the resampling correction using finite empirical guide averages. We prove that this correction exactly preserves the finite-particle block particle filter normalizer expectation, separating the effect of guided sampling from the approximation introduced by spatial blocking. Our analysis provides exact conditional local moments and a one-step conditional central limit result. We further derive explicit bounds on the correction accumulated across blocks and time, establish fixed-horizon consistency of the block filter and corrected normalizer under suitable regularity and guide-range conditions, and identify conditional criteria for guide perturbations that reduce variance. Experiments on coupled linear Gaussian and stochastic-volatility models with up to 256 latent dimensions show lower measured log-normalizer variance. For stochastic volatility with a five-step guide, the median reduction is $38\%$. An application to a 100-dimensional financial portfolio panel extends the evaluation to real data.

papers.title: TrustFlow-ECG: Reliability-Aware ECG Restoration with Calibrated Risk Estimation
papers.abstract: Electrocardiogram (ECG) restoration models can reduce noise and motion artifacts, but they rarely estimate whether the restored waveform is reliable for downstream analysis. We propose TrustFlow-ECG, a reliability-aware restoration framework that combines a one-step conditional rectified-flow restorer with a lightweight window-level risk predictor. The predictor uses the noisy ECG, restored ECG, and correction residual, then applies validation-set isotonic calibration for selective ECG analysis. We evaluate on MIT-BIH ECG windows corrupted with NSTDB artifacts, powerline interference, and mixed noise across multiple SNRs, with an external 9,675-window PTB-XL stress check without retraining. TrustFlow achieves 0.862 Spearman correlation with true risk and 0.911 AUROC for failure detection, while calibration reduces ECE from 0.0385 to 0.0098. At 80% coverage, selective rejection reduces RMSE from 0.1848 to 0.1345, improves R-peak F1 from 0.8778 to 0.9175, and reduces HR MAE from 6.26 to 4.88 bpm.

papers.title: A Closed-Form Soft Spectral Partition for Adaptive Mode Decomposition
papers.abstract: Density-based Adaptive Mode Decomposition (DAMD) shows that the Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD) objective, restricted to hard binary partitions, is equivalent to weighted K-means clustering, enabling automatic mode detection. The equivalence concerns detection only; extraction with hard Voronoi masks introduces boundary artefacts. This paper develops a soft extraction theory independent of the detector. First, the hard-partition equivalence is shown to be an algebraic identity that holds if and only if the weights are binary; hard and soft extraction are optima of two different functionals (linear K-means and regularised quadratic VMD) over the same simplex. Second, the regularised soft VMD problem is proved to have a closed-form global optimum, unique on the support of the spectrum: the Lorentzian-weighted partition $s_k^*(\omega)\propto[1+2\alpha(\omega-\omega_k)^2]^{-1}$. Every fixed point of the VMD ADMM mode update is proportional to $|\omega-\omega_k|^{-2}$; when the dual ascent enforces reconstruction, it is the $\alpha\to\infty$ endpoint of this family. The Lorentzian shape at finite $\alpha$ is therefore a consequence of the regulariser, and $\alpha$ controls how closely the allocation approaches that fixed point. Third, under a Lorentzian spectral prior the partition equals the minimum mean-square error (MMSE) estimator of each mode in the low-noise limit, tying $\alpha$ to the inverse squared mode bandwidth. Since the partition needs only detected centre frequencies, the extraction rule can be switched without recomputing detection. Synthetic experiments with known ground truth test the predictions; four categories of real signals show how much the two allocations differ.

papers.title: The generalized method of moments is (almost) statistically efficient in low-SNR Gaussian latent-variable models
papers.abstract: We study estimation in the low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) regime for a broad class of Gaussian latent-variable models, including Gaussian mixtures and orbit-recovery problems. We show that, in this regime, the generalized method-of-moments (GMoM) matches the first-order asymptotic efficiency of maximum likelihood. In particular, if the moment features are chosen up to the minimal local order required for identification and are weighted optimally, then the resulting GMoM estimator has the same leading asymptotic covariance as the maximum-likelihood estimator. We further show that this efficiency can be achieved using practical, data-driven weighting schemes and is preserved under a broad class of simpler weighting choices, including the commonly used identity-weighted method of moments, although these may incur larger higher-order efficiency losses. On the other hand, inappropriate weighting or discarding moment entries can lead to persistent efficiency losses even as SNR tends to zero, despite preserving identifiability. These results distinguish the moments required for identifiability from those needed for statistical efficiency, and characterize when moment-based estimation can match the performance of maximum likelihood.
